data.narrative:
SpectralX is a Series A–stage Defense & Security company founded by Asaf Picciotto and former IDF special-forces veterans. The valuation analysis draws on a comparable universe of 10 private companies and 2 public peers operating in the same sector and stage.

The peer-median method is the applicable triangulation approach given available data. Three same-sector, same-stage comparables—Stark Defence ($4.0B), Singularity ($400M), and NODA AI ($125M)—yield a median valuation of $400M. The dispersion is material: the range spans $125M to $4.0B, reflecting variance in business model maturity, customer traction, and capital intensity within early-stage defense tech. This peer median anchors the valuation framework.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $340M to $460M, with a median of $400M. Key uncertainties include the absence of revenue or customer contract data, which limits application of revenue multiple or cash-flow-based methods. The wide spread among peer valuations ($125M–$4.0B) underscores heterogeneity in how defense-tech Series A companies are priced. Without visibility into SpectralX's customer pipeline, technology defensibility, or capital requirements, the range should be treated as indicative rather than prescriptive. Additional diligence on customer wins and gross margins would narrow this band.
